summary: Retested header sign-out UX after redesign (plain red Sign out button replaced by top-right avatar user-menu). 4 new browser checks cover the updated acceptance matrix (menu visibility/contents, both sign-out paths, change-password-from-menu, mobile). All passed. 5 obsolete checks from iteration_19 that asserted the old flat header-logout-button (visible without opening the menu) now fail against the new UI by design and were retired/removed per the briefing's spec_deviations note rather than reported as bugs.

checks.criterion: Top-right user menu with sign out (like professional apps) plus sidebar bottom sign out
checks.name: header-user-menu-visible-and-contents
checks.evidence: Logged in as kumararaja, qaagent, bo2001 at 1400x800 and 1366x640; header-user-menu visible top-right each time, sidebar logout-button visible bottom-left; clicking header-user-menu revealed header-change-password and header-logout-button menu items. 6 screenshots captured.

checks.name: both-signout-paths-work
checks.evidence: As qaagent at 1400x800: opened header-user-menu -> clicked header-logout-button -> redirected to /login; visiting / afterwards redirected back to /login. Logged in again, clicked sidebar logout-button -> redirected to /login; visiting / again redirected to /login. Both paths verified independently.

checks.name: header-change-password-opens-dialog
checks.evidence: As kumararaja at 1400x800: opened header-user-menu, clicked header-change-password, change-password dialog (role=dialog) became visible.

checks.name: mobile-header-user-menu-signout
checks.evidence: At 390x844 as qaagent: header-user-menu (avatar) visible, opened menu, header-logout-button visible and clicking it redirected to /login.

action_items.detail: Removed 5 obsolete browser checks from iteration_19 (logout-visible-desktop-multi-role, logout-ends-session-redirects-login, logout-visible-mobile-viewport, logout-preview-ingress-smoke, sidebar-nav-and-search-no-regression) that asserted header-logout-button was directly visible in the header without opening a menu. Per briefing spec_deviations, this is the intended redesign (button now lives inside header-user-menu), not a regression. Their underlying flows (sign-out works, mobile sign-out, nav regression, preview-ingress smoke) are now covered by the 4 new checks above except plain nav-regression and preview-ingress smoke, which were not re-authored since they are not in the current acceptance_matrix; re-add if nav-regression/ingress-smoke coverage is still desired going forward.
